**Missouri seniors need property tax relief _NOW_**
Dear neighbor,

Legislation that safeguards Missouri's seniors and keeps them in their homes has always been a top priority of mine. This year, my [SJR 41 - Senior property tax relief bill](https://robertsforstl.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6e3f7ee3b541518ea63c7e773&id=7373986830&e=a088917f89) has passed the Missouri Senate with overwhelming bipartisan support. Unfortunately, Missouri House leadership refuse to put it on the floor for a vote. With only two legislative weeks remaining, I need _YOUR_ help to get it across the finish line.

I ask that supporters of senior tax relief contact House leadership and demand [SJR 41](https://robertsforstl.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6e3f7ee3b541518ea63c7e773&id=2970ea5990&e=a088917f89) be voted on and passed. It is unfair that our seniors, the stalwarts of our communities, are being driven from their homes because they can no longer afford the rapidly rising property taxes.

Thank you and take care.
**Speaker of the House**
Rob Vescovo (R)

| **Senate passes budget to set up final negotiations with House**
The Senate on April 26 approved its version of the FY 2023 state operating budget, adding more than $1 billion in additional spending authority over what the House of Representatives has approved. The two chambers must now negotiate a final spending plan with just days to go until the May 6 constitutional deadline for completing the budget.

But while the main appropriations bills are on a path to final passage, separate $2.58 billion spending measure to allocate federal pandemic relief funds has stalled in the Senate Appropriations Committee, which on April 27 abruptly cancelled two planned meetings that had been scheduled to work on the bill. With an extremely tight timetable to send the main budget bills to the governor, it rapidly becoming less likely lawmakers will have time to finalize how the pandemic relief funds should be spent. In that event, the governor could call a special legislative session for lawmakers to finish the job after the regular session ends on May 13.

Excluding that bill, the Senate version of the operating budget includes $45.1 billion in spending authority – substantially more than the $43.9 billion House version. As a result, House and Senate negotiators have many points of disagreement to work out.

Key Senate additions include an additional $214 million to fully fund the state’s share of local public school districts’ student transportation costs for the first time in three decades, plus $27 million to increase minimum pay for public school teachers to $38,000 a year. While Republican House budget leaders excluded funding for both from their budget plan, those items are popular among lawmakers of both political parties and could be difficult to remove during negotiations.

| **House approves allowing workers to sue over vaccinations**
Legislation that would allow workers to sue their employers over vaccinations barely passed the House of Representatives on April 25 on a vote of 84-58, winning just two more “yes” votes than required to advance to the Senate.

House Bill 1692 would create a legal cause of action for workers to sue their employers if they suffer a negative reaction to any vaccine there are required to take as a condition of employment. Although legislation targeting COVID-19 vaccine mandates have been popular in the majority-Republican Missouri General Assembly this year, HB 1692 is unusual because it would allow lawsuits over vaccinations against any disease, including those that have been commonly required for decades.

The state’s major business groups, which typically lean Republican, all opposed the bill, prompting a handful of GOP lawmakers to join Democrats in opposition. Democrats noted that any injuries resulting from vaccines required for employment already are covered by the state workers’ compensation system.
---
|
---
| **House advances bill attempting to nullify federal election law**
The House of Representatives on April 28 voted 96-47-1 to advance legislation to the Senate that purports to allow the state to ignore federal election laws, fine election officials who follow federal law without legislative approval and impose a photo voter identification requirement, which the Missouri Supreme Court has twice struck down as unconstitutional.

The wide-ranging House Bill 2140 includes a provision purporting to empower the Missouri General Assembly to decide what federal election laws the state will follow. A related provision seeks to impose fines of $5,000 per month on election officials who follow federal law without legislative approval. In addition, accepting federal election funding without permission could result in a $1,000 fine, plus the amount of funding received. These provisions likely violate the U.S. Constitution’s Supremacy Clause, under which federal laws trump conflicting state laws.

The Republican-backed bill also seeks to require voters to show a government-issued photo ID in an effort to disenfranchise racial minorities and members of other groups that tend to support Democrats and are most likely not to have a photo ID. In striking down similar laws in the past, the state Supreme Court has noted there has never been a documented case voter impersonation at the polls in Missouri, yet that is the only type of voter fraud a photo ID requirement could prevent. As a result, the court has said such laws fail to clear the high constitutional bar for restricting Missourians’ fundamental right to vote.

During debate on the bill, Republicans added an amendment to allow each public school district to put a measure on the local ballot that, if approved by voters, would ban transgender girls from participating in girls’ sports, even though over the last decade few transgender girls have sought to play on girls’ teams in Missouri.
---
|
---
| **Supreme Court revives challenge to controversial gun law**
The Missouri Supreme Court on April 26 revived a lawsuit challenging a controversial state law that purports to declare federal gun laws unenforceable in Missouri and punishes local police departments for assisting federal authorities in criminal investigations.

In its 6-1 ruling, the high court majority said Cole County Circuit Judge Dan Green, a Republican, erred when he determined the plaintiffs’ legal claims weren’t ripe for consideration. The majority ordered Green to consider the merits of plaintiffs’ constitutional arguments. In a solo dissent, Judge Zel Fischer said the plaintiffs have alternate avenues to pursue their claims.

At issue is House Bill 85, which the Republican-controlled General Assembly enacted in 2021. In addition to purporting to nullify federal gun laws, HB 85 authorizes federal gun offenders to sue Missouri police departments for a minimum $50,000 per occurrence, plus attorney fees, for assisting federal authorities. The bill also subjects any local government agency to similar fines merely for hiring a former federal agent who previously enforced gun laws, regardless of whether that person is hired in a law enforcement capacity. The law is dubiously referred to as the “Second Amendment Preservation Act.”

St. Louis city, St. Louis County and Jackson County jointly sued to stop enforcement of the law, claiming it violates the U.S. Constitution’s Supremacy Clause, which prohibits individual states from invalidating federal laws. In an uncommon move, the U.S. Department of Justice later joined the case in support of the plaintiffs, arguing HB 85 has chilled cooperation between state and federal law enforcement officials in criminal investigations.

Regardless of how the trial judge ultimately rules on remand, the case is again expected to be appealed to the state Supreme Court. The case is _City of St. Louis, St. Louis County and Jackson County v. State of Missouri._

The majority ordered Green to consider the merits of plaintiffs’ constitutional arguments. In a solo dissent, Judge Zel Fischer said the plaintiffs have alternate avenues to pursue their claims. At issue is House Bill 85, which the Republican-controlled General Assembly enacted in 2021. In addition to purporting to nullify federal gun laws, HB 85 authorizes federal gun offenders to sue Missouri police departments for a minimum $50,000 per occurrence, plus attorney fees, for assisting federal authorities. The bill also subjects any local government agency to similar fines merely for hiring a former federal agent who previously enforced gun laws, regardless of whether that person is hired in a law enforcement capacity. The law is dubiously referred to as the “Second Amendment Preservation Act.” St. Louis city, St. Louis County and Jackson County jointly sued to stop enforcement of the law, claiming it violates the U.S. Constitution’s Supremacy Clause, which prohibits individual states from invalidating federal laws. In an uncommon move, the U.S. Department of Justice later joined the case in support of the plaintiffs, arguing HB 85 has chilled cooperation between state and federal law enforcement officials in criminal investigations. Regardless of how the trial judge ultimately rules on remand, the case is again expected to be appealed to the state Supreme Court. The case is City of St. Louis, St. Louis County and Jackson County v. body:
Here's why McCarthy's lies were so shocking. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44725179/342837012/390307162?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTYyOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMWI1Y2YwMS1mOGM3LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dMUH-lJGAmPmhECJXOBZ3EEKEgyWudp0UARYAyaVOTA=)
Friend,

I'm sure you saw the news that Kevin McCarthy -- the man who would hold the Speaker's gavel if Republicans take the House -- lied about planning to call on Trump to resign after Jan 6th.

McCarthy's instinct in the aftermath of Jan 6th was to hold Donald Trump accountable. But that sentiment was almost immediately overruled by his desire to become Speaker of the House. **That's what's so shocking about this controversy. body:
| | | [](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/f8b06988627a68f8c3d6b838967d376c/37793)
---
Friend, **EARLY VOTING STARTS ON MONDAY! ** The fourth quarter is here, and we’re leaving it all on the field. We’re continuing to barnstorm Georgia, our Team ’22 members are continuing to contact voters in their communities every single day, and this week we released our first TV ad. None of this would be possible without your prayers and support! [**We’re humbled by that, and if you’re able, I hope you’ll consider a contribution to help fuel our efforts in the weeks ahead.**](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/aa22677f9874c4d0c3d6b838967d376c/37793)
---
---
# _**Early Voting**_
---
|
---
[](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/ce7b75c36df099fac3d6b838967d376c/37793)
---
As mentioned above, Monday marks the official start of early voting in Georgia! We’re counting on each of you to go to the polls and cast your ballot — and bring 22 of your friends with you. **[Our team has put together a Voter Resources page that’s a one-stop shop for everything you need to know about voting.](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/848a1eb1f736282dc3d6b838967d376c/37793)** Hope you’ll use it as a resource as you plan when you’re going to vote.
---
---
# **_Open Border_**

---
[| | |
---|---|---](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/b398b27c1790605cc3d6b838967d376c/37793)
This week, we launched our first television spot of the campaign. It highlights the crisis at our southern border, how Joe Biden and Raphael Warnock’s policies created it, and how stopping it is going to take more than another status quo Republican. This ad is going to continue airing across Georgia, and I hope you’ll personally share it with each of your contacts.
---
---
# _**Closing Argument State Tour**_
---
[](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/8ff9395389308b61c3d6b838967d376c/37793)
---
From Chattahoochee Hills to Bartow County, Norcross to Ringgold... B.I.G. crowds have joined us at each of our stops this week! We must nominate a Republican who will show up, hear what’s on the voters’ hearts, answer the tough questions, and who won’t be outworked.
---
---
# **_Atlanta Press Club Debate_**
---
[](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/322836b4c98e1071c3d6b838967d376c/37793)
---
On WEDNESDAY, I’ll participate in the Atlanta Press Club’s debate. Looking forward to a serious discussion of the issues and sharing why trusted experienced — not celebrity — will defeat Raphael Warnock in November. The debate will be live on GPB from 7:00-8:00 pm and streamed live on [**The Atlanta Press Club’s Facebook Page**](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/2f9fd9cc290a0426c3d6b838967d376c/37793) and **[GPB.org](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/0e82897e342bb71a041ad8cde91a9694/37793/ea1b884f483dbabd/760591cbc2c4908ac3d6b838967d376c/37793)**. It will also be available online on GPB and Atlanta Press Club social media afterwards. Hope you’ll tune in!
---
---

Delegate Robbyn Lewis and former Delegate Salima Marriott Gibbs are dedicated changemakers, and we are so grateful to have their support. Delegate Pat Young is a dedicated and impactful member of the Maryland General Assembly. subject: Why AZ Taxpayers Are Relieved
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ducey for Governor
body:
Arizona Chamber President & CEO on what's happening with your taxes, and why it's good news | |
---
| | |
---
| | | Hello,

The President & CEO of Arizona's Chamber of Commerce writes this week about Arizona's tax policy under Gov. Ducey and how years of balanced budgets and tax cuts are helping Arizonans keep more of what they earn.

Read the full op-ed:
---
| [ ](https://dougducey.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=bf4fbf102e325035a83ef3427&id=ffb698d7de&e=55d4e2f84a)
---
| The state Supreme Court has ruled that the historic income tax reduction passed by the Legislature and signed by Gov. Ducey last year will not be referred to the November ballot. That means Arizona is on its way to having a simple, low, fair and flat state income tax of 2.5% –the lowest in the nation. But it’s worth remembering how we got to this point. In 2014, Arizona was fighting to emerge from the Great Recession, hit harder than almost every state in the country. We were staring down a billion-dollar budget deficit

I was on the campaign trail for then-candidate Doug Ducey when he made a pledge that, to many, may have sounded like a pipe dream – as governor, he would make Arizona the No. 1 state to live, work, and start and run a business – all while reducing the state income tax to as close to zero as possible.

Skeptics mocked the idea, believing it wasn’t possible. Opponents called instead for higher taxes, claiming his plan would bankrupt Arizona. Cynics, perhaps disillusioned by years of empty promises, assumed they were being fed another speech by an ambitious politician who’d say anything to get elected. All stump, no substance.

Undeterred, Governor Ducey was elected – not once, but twice – and he has been delivering on those promises since Day One. I’ve known our governor a long time. And if there’s one thing you should know, it’s that his administration is about results – not rhetoric. And the results speak for themselves.

Fast forward to today. Arizona has dug itself out of a $1 billion hole, and now sits on a record $5 billion surplus. Our economy is booming. Our population is growing. Since taking office, Arizona has welcomed 18,000 new businesses and over half-a-million new residents. We’ve created almost 400,000 new jobs and recovered those lost during the pandemic faster than nearly every other state. Our 3.3% unemployment rate, better than the national average, represents a historic low not seen in over 45 years.

All of this, while pumping record investments into K-12 education, supporting vital infrastructure needs, and funding core priorities like public safety, health care and more. All of this, while cutting taxes every year and advancing pro-growth policies that have made our state among the most competitive in the nation.

None of this was by accident. The current circumstances reflect 7-plus years of good policy and relentless salesmanship by a leader who had a strong vision for what our economy could be. And as for that campaign promise? Last session, Governor Ducey championed and signed into law a historic tax reform package that slashed rates for every Arizona taxpayer and implemented a 2.5% flat rate – the lowest among all other states with an income tax.

The fate of that plan hung in limbo over recent months, as opponents attempted to overturn it via a voter referendum. Thankfully, the Arizona Supreme Court blocked those efforts, rightfully recognizing our Constitution does not allow for the referral of tax measures that impact the “support and maintenance” of state government.

This would be a win for Arizona taxpayers and small businesses under any circumstance, never mind during this period of unprecedented inflation. This decision provides relief for every Arizonan who finds themselves spending more than ever before to fill up their cars, put food on the table, and shelter and clothe their families – and yes, that’s every Arizonan. It also provides the much-needed certainty that Arizona will have the lowest flat-tax rate in the nation – keeping our business environment among the most attractive and competitive for job creators and ensuring the continued long-term economic growth of our state.

We’re grateful to Governor Ducey and the state Legislature for delivering on a promise that Arizonans can take to the bank.

_Danny Seiden is president and CEO of the Arizona Chamber of Commerce and Industry. _

# **Newsletter-April 29 Vol. 2, #10**
---
| | |
##
29 April 22

**Only 11 Weeks Until The July 19 Primary.**
Although Jeff has two primary competitors, they are not campaigning or fundraising, yet we will not take anything for granted and we are actively and tirelessly campaigning...And **We Need Your Help!** The options are easy!

**In Person Meet & Greet**
The campaign recently covered over 1550 homes reaching Primary Voters in Beltsville, Burtonsville & Laurel.
Another Meet & Greet is scheduled for Thursday, May 5, 7-8p at Mission BBQ in Laurel.
14712 Baltimore Ave, Laurel, 20707
This is a great opportunity to learn more about our winning strategy and how to get involved.
Invite others to attend (especially if you've attended a Meet & Greet), to meet and hear from Jeff!

**Sign Waving - One Power Hour**
THIS, Saturday, April 30, you're invited to sign wave for one power hour with the Jeff Warner For Congress campaign.
Noon-1p
Route 1 & Cherry Hill Road in College Park
You should be able to park in the large parking lot near Starbucks
4750 Cherry Hill Rd, College Park, 20740
Please park as far as possible from the buildings so we don't limit customer access.
Let's meet at the intersection of Route 1 & Cherry Hill Rd.
You should see Jeff there.

If you have a sign, please bring it. If you have a sign and are not planning on sign waving or posting, please let us know so we can put it to use and stretch our limited funds. Consider dressing layers and bring your BIG smile.
.
**Phone Calling**
A BIG THANK YOU, to everyone who is calling! We're making GREAT progress.

Please keep in mind, around 2% of calls, involve speaking with voters. The goal is to introduce the campaign through a pre-recorded message from Jeff Warner, their next Congressman, to the voter's voicemail.

You can make an impact no matter where you live in the nation. Please email the campaign at info@JeffWarnerForCongress.com if you’re in interested in getting trained. It's easy.

**Important Details:**
Phone calls are audio only, no video.
A sample script is provided.
The system is all online. Anyone in the USA can assist.
Serve from home (or anyplace you'd like). There is no call center.
Your phone and phone number are not used and are therefore protected.
You choose how much you'd like to call.

**Social Media**
The campaign is taking steps to build Jeff Warner's social media presence.
You can find Jeff under RepJeffWarner on Facebook (https://www.facebook.com/RepJeffWarner) & Twitter (@RepJeff Warner).
Be sure to like, share, subscribe, follow, etc. to help us grow his following.

Thank You for your support. The campaign continues to make and break records. Come and be a part of this amazing team. Imagine how good it will be to say you were part of this team in November as we celebrate our historic victory!

[**Donate Here**](https://gmail.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e2b757c427e67a891eab3e1b8&id=86fa2297f4&e=12a37459a2)

Remember, Jeff Warner is standing with you and for you. Enough is Enough! Together, "We The People" can make a real difference. Now is our time to act. THERE IS HOPE!

Standing with you,

Jeff

_**"I make a hard distinction between Black conservatives and these tokens [Herschel Walker and Senator Tim Scott], who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers."**
--Eli Mystal, MSNBC_

Peter,

I recently wrote to you about a racist article attacking me in _The Nation_.

The author had some pretty heinous things to say because I'm a Black conservative. You may recall this line:

_"Herschel Walker's candidacy is a white insult to Black people."_

**That's racist, disgusting, and sad.**

#
Derek,
To be honest, the uptick in online donations we *typically* see near the end of the month just isn't where we projected.

**[According to our calculations, we can still meet our goal before midnight if around 16 more folks from 18326 are able to chip in. Can we put you down for a last-minute $5 donation today? **\- Four Ways the American Rescue Plan Delivered for Hoosiers this Week - **
1. **Muncie Teachers Get Their Raise - Thanks to the American Rescue Plan** President Joe Biden’s [American Rescue Plan](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44728351/342849433/2075701864?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMmFkMjI3ZS0wMWM4LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XYJQEr0U4GJqoc0dFecZKHkJWRWpisKSFPauCUvDLto=&emci=c94415a2-f2c7-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&emdi=22ad227e-01c8-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&ceid=4925535) provided teachers in Muncie a much-needed pay raise. This increase will begin at the start of the 2022-23 school year, and it will effectively “[make Muncie into one of the top-paying school districts in the state](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44728353/342849437/-1192348192?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMmFkMjI3ZS0wMWM4LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XYJQEr0U4GJqoc0dFecZKHkJWRWpisKSFPauCUvDLto=&emci=c94415a2-f2c7-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&emdi=22ad227e-01c8-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&ceid=4925535)”. Indiana Democrats like André Carson and Frank Mrvan voted “YES” to provide the state about $5.8 billion via the Rescue Plan. This investment nearly doubled the state budget for 2021-22 year - securing a pay raise for teachers that was originally left out. Teachers would not have received their raise without the help of the [American Rescue Plan](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44728355/342849440/-1119998622?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMmFkMjI3ZS0wMWM4LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XYJQEr0U4GJqoc0dFecZKHkJWRWpisKSFPauCUvDLto=&emci=c94415a2-f2c7-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&emdi=22ad227e-01c8-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&ceid=4925535), and it’s Indiana Democrats who got it done.
2. **INGOP Commissioner: American Rescue Plan’s Broadband Dollars a “Big, Big Winner” for Hoosier Families in Bartholomew County**

The ARP provided about $4 million to expand broadband access for families – making Bartholomew County a “[big, big winner](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44728356/342849441/-68226001?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMmFkMjI3ZS0wMWM4LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XYJQEr0U4GJqoc0dFecZKHkJWRWpisKSFPauCUvDLto=&emci=c94415a2-f2c7-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&emdi=22ad227e-01c8-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&ceid=4925535)” according to Republican (and County Commissioner) Tony London.

---
Hi Peter, Honestly, I don’t know what happened to the month of April. The month flew by, and it was the busiest at the Capitol in years. Committee hearings were nonstop, and we killed the three worst mandate bills. As a result, I wasn’t able to spend the time needed to campaign in a competitive race for Congress just before voting starts. It’s so important that we make up for that now. [Here is the donation link](https://kevinkiley.nationbuilder.com/r?u=09K6E4GvoPozZ73mzf50y5etLj1_9wCfyRoQ3wvVmv-GOhHPWzgYbh54Gph7Pyuk3g2mp41Qa8XyLKk0CnWqFcPhfo-70bh2d9FGRmWv-G172QGsW76cwQP_qMTr_tK1&e=eff202566bfe6143aa18c9c627e100fe&utm_source=kevinkiley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=apr29_final&n=2), but I want to give you a sense of the political situation as we face this end-of-month deadline. Ballots will start arriving next week. This is the only open seat for Congress in a Republican district in California. It’s a once-in-a-generation opportunity. And we are in the lead. That is truly exciting; it’s a testament to the power of our citizens movement. If we can keep reaching voters on the air, in the mail, and on social media through Election Day, we will win. But if we have to make cuts, we might lose. [Please help assure that we don’t have to make any damaging cuts](https://kevinkiley.nationbuilder.com/r?u=09K6E4GvoPozZ73mzf50y5etLj1_9wCfyRoQ3wvVmv-GOhHPWzgYbh54Gph7Pyuk3g2mp41Qa8XyLKk0CnWqFcPhfo-70bh2d9FGRmWv-G172QGsW76cwQP_qMTr_tK1&e=eff202566bfe6143aa18c9c627e100fe&utm_source=kevinkiley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=apr29_final&n=3). We’ve worked so hard to get to this point, but all could be lost if we don’t make our budget. If we have to cut back on our positive messaging, there will be a vacuum – and our opponents will fill it with negative attacks. These opponents are Pelosi and the national Democrats, the swamp creatures of both parties, and now the press. [I need your help to make sure our opponents do not succeed](https://kevinkiley.nationbuilder.com/r?u=09K6E4GvoPozZ73mzf50y5etLj1_9wCfyRoQ3wvVmv-GOhHPWzgYbh54Gph7Pyuk3g2mp41Qa8XyLKk0CnWqFcPhfo-70bh2d9FGRmWv-G172QGsW76cwQP_qMTr_tK1&e=eff202566bfe6143aa18c9c627e100fe&utm_source=kevinkiley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=apr29_final&n=4)**.** If we were to fall short, I have no doubt that our movement would still continue. I am just one person. But I want to be in the fight with you. I want to help our movement grow. I want to fight against Biden just as hard as I’ve fought against Newsom. I want to be a national voice for all California conservatives and patriots. I want to continue my blog, reporting to you on what is really going on in the U.S. Capitol. I won’t be able to do that if our opponents knock me out these next few weeks. That’s why today [I’m asking for your support](https://kevinkiley.nationbuilder.com/r?u=09K6E4GvoPozZ73mzf50y5etLj1_9wCfyRoQ3wvVmv-GOhHPWzgYbh54Gph7Pyuk3g2mp41Qa8XyLKk0CnWqFcPhfo-70bh2d9FGRmWv-G172QGsW76cwQP_qMTr_tK1&e=eff202566bfe6143aa18c9c627e100fe&utm_source=kevinkiley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=apr29_final&n=5), in the highest amount you can afford. I know I am asking a lot, but it will make all the difference. I’m so grateful for whatever help you can provide. Thank you so much, and let’s win this race. Kevin p.s. I know you are prudent with your funds and get a lot of emails, so I try to only send you a direct request when it’s most important. It’s more important than ever right now. [Here is the link](https://kevinkiley.nationbuilder.com/r?u=09K6E4GvoPozZ73mzf50y5etLj1_9wCfyRoQ3wvVmv-GOhHPWzgYbh54Gph7Pyuk3g2mp41Qa8XyLKk0CnWqFcPhfo-70bh2d9FGRmWv-G172QGsW76cwQP_qMTr_tK1&e=eff202566bfe6143aa18c9c627e100fe&utm_source=kevinkiley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=apr29_final&n=6) one more time.

# EARLY VOTING

### Greetings!

Please make a plan and go vote! Your voice will be what determines our tomorrow.
Early voting has started and because it is a non-Presidental primary almost half of the votes are cast in comparison to Presidential primaries.
We cannot let less than 10% of the electorate decide whom we are represented by. Democracy is about citizens being engaged in the process.

I humbly ask for your vote!

Elissa Slotkin for Congresssecure.actblue.com/donate/slotkinq22022?refcode=email20220429&amount=28 [secure.actblue.com/donate/slotkinq22022?refcode=email20220429&amount=28]
Team,
It’s hard to believe we’re just a day away from May – it feels like we were just discussing our New Year’s resolutions. Good lord.
Today, we wanted to lay out the case for a central part of our fundraising: the monthly donations. We currently have over 1,000 monthly donors contributing an amount per month that makes sense for them. For some its $1, for others it's $10, and for some it's even $100.
We know it’s an unusual thing to ask, but here’s why it’s important: it provides wonderful, glorious predictability. Monthly donors allow us to predict a baseline of funding every month.
Here’s why this is important: one thing we need to do between now and Election Day is purchase television ad time for the fall. Buying these slots ahead of time allows us to choose the best time slots for our ads to air: we want the television blocks with higher viewership. We also have to write, film, and edit these ads – which is both costly and time consuming from start to finish.
Another big priority this summer? Building up our ground game for the fall. We’ll be recruiting new volunteers, hitting the doors to talk to voters, and hosting “friend-raisers” so Elissa can connect with new networks of Democratic supporters in the new district.
Things will really start kicking into gear after August 2nd – Michigan’s Primary Election Day. The months following the August primary will be the high-stress final push to make it to Election Day in November. We’ll have volunteers knocking doors, making phone calls, and distributing yard signs. MSU students will return to campus in the fall, and it will be an all out effort from Team Slotkin and our “Students for Slotkin” group to drive turnout amongst college students – a task that is easier said than done!
This final push will be when all of the work we’ve put in during these early months pays off – and why we’re asking if you will chip in monthly to help us get there.
If you’re game to contribute monthly, click on the “contribute” link below, select whatever amount you’re comfortable with, and then check “Yes, count me in!” under “make it monthly.” [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/slotkinq22022?refcode=email20220429&amount=28]
Not ready to commit to a monthly contribution yet? That’s ok! You can use the same link to make a one-time contribution to one of the most competitive races in the country! [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/slotkinq22022?refcode=email20220429&amount=28]

Peter, we have
good news and bad news.

We’ll start with the bad: Right now, we’re only 82% of the way toward
reaching our April fundraising goal and there’s less than 48 hours until
the deadline.

We thought that we’d be further along by now and it’s especially important
since our primary is only weeks away. We can’t afford to fall short on
this goal.

But here’s the good news: We’re cutting it close — but if just half of the
people reading this email chips in we can catch up in time.

donations? Every dollar you give will power our last big push before the
primary to remind Kentuckians to vote, share Charles’ message for change
with undecided voters, and give support to folks who need help getting to
the polls.

a pivotal moment for our campaign.

body:
With just one day until our deadline, this is what we need.
# [](https://act.morganharper.org/go/1512?refcode=em20220429-1016-footer-ak&t=2&akid=1016%2E90090%2EFWyl-d)
We’re in the final stretch before the primary now.
There’s just ONE day until our final, pre-primary reporting deadline at midnight on April 30 and only FOUR days until the primary election. Because this campaign is fueled by grassroots donations, not corporate PAC money, this deadline is crucially important to getting out the vote before polls close on May 3rd.
That’s why I’m asking you directly: **[Can you chip in $5 right now to help us reach our pre-primary fundraising goal and get out the vote in every community across Ohio?](https://act.morganharper.org/go/33033?t=3&akid=1016%2E90090%2EFWyl-d)**
**[Contribute $5](https://act.morganharper.org/go/33039?refcode=em20220429-1016&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=1016%2E90090%2EFWyl-d)**
Look, I’m running for Senate because our communities here in Ohio are suffering, people are tired of the status quo, and we need each other now more than ever. I know because I grew up the daughter of an immigrant in a strong community that looked out for one another.
I look around our state now and I see so many communities that used to be like that — communities that with the right leadership and the right support, could be vibrant and connected once again.
So I don’t need corporations or the establishment to tell me what policies would help our state. **That’s why this campaign has relied on grassroots donations from day one, and why we really need our supporters — people like YOU — to step up in this critical final stretch.**
**[There are less than 36 hours until our deadline and we can’t let a single moment go to waste — so can you make a contribution right now to help power our team through Election Day?](https://act.morganharper.org/go/33033?t=23&akid=1016%2E90090%2EFWyl-d)**
Thank you for all that you do!
Together,
Morgan

Peter,

I got involved in politics for the same reason so many other women do – I was mad.

People told me that I couldn’t make a difference. One male legislator even said I was “just a mom in tennis shoes.” I had two choices. I could admit defeat or show him just how far these tennis shoes could carry me. And here’s the thing about moms – we’re always tougher than you think.

Since then, I’ve been fighting for every mom and family in Washington state by leading important fights in the Senate – like ending the child care crisis, guaranteeing paid family leave, and lowering health care costs.

But we only have a razor-thin majority, and the GOP are determined to not only block our agenda that puts families first but also win back control of Congress in November.

**[Peter, will you rush in $10 to my campaign and Kim Schrier’s right now to keep Congress blue and stop Mitch McConnell and Kevin McCarthy from erasing all of our progress?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44722337/342823669/1331311596?refcode=em22_220427_eom5_fnd_gq_act___pm_ettx&utm_campaign=em22_220427_eom5_fnd_gq_act___pm_ettx&utm_medium=email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmOWYyZjBhNi1lZWM3LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3ZdIn6RiZnzAe7eCNwfeM2JxI2wYJJTVCve8t4cWNlE=)**

I go to work every day in the other Washington to fight for families like yours and make sure your voices are heard. **Republicans don’t like me for just that reason – and that’s why they’re targeting Washington state as a seat to flip this November.**

Republicans only need **_ONE_** seat to retake the Senate majority so it’s critical we do everything we can to win this race in Washington state and defend and expand our Democratic majorities in both the House and Senate.

**[If there’s one thing I know for sure, it’s how powerful our voices can be when we join together – so I’m counting on you to contribute $10 to my campaign and Kim’s now.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44722339/342823671/1331311596?refcode=em22_220427_eom5_fnd_gq_act___pm_ettx&utm_campaign=em22_220427_eom5_fnd_gq_act___pm_ettx&utm_medium=email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmOWYyZjBhNi1lZWM3LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3ZdIn6RiZnzAe7eCNwfeM2JxI2wYJJTVCve8t4cWNlE=)**

Thank you for your support,

Sen. Patty Murray (D-WA)

| | Our greatest community resources - Nuestros mayores recursos comunitarios
---
| |
---
| | Nuestro futuro en el centro de Washington será brillante, pero aún queda trabajo por hacer. Como líder electo, apoyaré programas que promuevan comunidades seguras; y reducir la falta de vivienda, la violencia y el abuso de drogas. Apoyaré los programas que crean una economía sólida al preparar a nuestros niños para que tengan éxito. Como empresario, sé que cuando construimos prisiones más rápido que escuelas y gastamos 3 veces más para encarcelar a alguien de lo que gastamos en educarlo, el problema NO es una policía insuficiente. El Departamento de Policía de Yakima ha iniciado una serie de programas centrados en mantener a los niños alejados de la delincuencia mediante el trabajo con otras organizaciones gubernamentales y comunitarias locales. Cuando incluso la policía ha reconocido que asignar sus recursos para mantener a los niños alejados de la delincuencia es más valioso para la comunidad que encarcelarlos después de que es demasiado tarde, entonces es hora de que nuestros líderes electos se unan a esto. Si alguien le pregunta, ¿preferiría gastar un poco más de dinero ahora y sentirse seguro en su hogar o gastar mucho más dinero más adelante y seguir viendo cómo la violencia y el abuso de drogas destrozan su comunidad, qué respondería? Sé qué elección tomaré; la decisión fiscalmente responsable y moralmente correcta.
---
| Our future in Central Washington will be bright, but there is still work to be done. As an elected leader I will support programs that promote safe communities; and reduce homelessness, violence, and drug abuse. I will support programs that create a strong economy by preparing our kids to be successful. As a businessman I know that when we build prisons faster than schools and spend 3X more to incarcerate someone than we spend on educating them, the problem is NOT insufficient police. The Yakima Police Department has started a number of programs focused on keeping kids off a criminal path by working with other local government and community organizations. When even the police have recognized that allocating their resources to keeping kids off a criminal path is of greater value to the community than to incarcerate after it is too late, then it is time for our elected leaders to get on board with this. If someone asks you, would you rather spend a little more money now and feel safe in your homes or spend a lot more money later and continue to see violence and drug abuse tear apart your community, how would you answer? I know which choice I will make; the fiscally responsible and morally correct decision.

name: Alessandra Biaggi
subject: An update on Congressional maps.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alessandra Biaggi for Congress
body:
#
Hi Friends —
By now, many of you know that the New York State Court of Appeals threw out the new Congressional and State Senate maps that were implemented earlier this year.
**I’m reaching out today to personally explain how that changes the state of our race.**
Here’s what’s next:
* First, a liaison appointed by the court will redraw the lines of the district. This will mean that the primaries will be pushed from June to August, with the date to be determined.

I wanted to tell you about my grandmother –
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44734838/342876377/-947982778?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=mh-jtk971-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NGEwY2YzZC0xOWM4LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MAYPo-nPvg95o6TuN9BAO74JLYgjK8Ava8pLLtQvNl0=) My grandmother turned 22 years old on June 4, 1919 – the same day the U.S. Senate passed the 19th Amendment, the beginning of the fight to guarantee voting rights for all American women.

I think a lot about what it must have been like for my grandmother to grow up never expecting to have the right to vote.
My grandmother wasn't a highly political person; she just believed in including people and in making things work. But she always took her right to vote very seriously, and always made sure she exercised that right on Election Day.

She understood, as we all need to, that we can't take the right to vote for granted. We need to ensure that everyone has the right to vote and that we protect that right with everything we have.
Every day, I'm inspired by the women who came before me – my mother, my grandmother, my great-grandmother – who understood the magnitude of casting their ballot and who taught us the importance of working to make our democracy more inclusive and accessible.
**As Senator, I'm fighting for our shared values each and every day: expanding access to the ballot box, protecting reproductive health care, and lowering costs for families – but I can't do it alone. **
My last election was the closest in the country, and this year could be even closer. Losing even one Senate seat means losing our Senate majority, and Republicans are doing everything they can to end our majority by targeting my seat.

| | | Dear friends, I shared the news with delegates at the Seventh Congressional District convention today that I made the decision this week to suspend my campaign for Governor.

[**I recorded a video message that I'd like to share with you about my decision.**](https://michelle4mn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0e599d2cf739987622330d245&id=bec0a31e3d&e=9d6926af69) I’m thankful to my husband Craig, my children Calvin, Grant, and Claire, extended family, and the countless volunteers who stood with me in this effort. **I’m beyond grateful for your efforts to create a place we are proud to call home and look forward to working together in the future.**

[](https://michelle4mn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0e599d2cf739987622330d245&id=c073f5b5b7&e=9d6926af69)

Over the next several days, I will be taking the time to connect with family and friends. **I look forward to seeing you at the state convention and unifying behind a candidate that can defeat Tim Walz this fall.**

Your friend,

Jane Timken for Ohio Update| | | [](https://)
---
| | Dear Peter, As we head into the last weekend of the campaign, Jane continues to work hard to earn the vote of Ohio Republican primary voters. With 35 events over the last 12 days of the campaign, Jane is crisscrossing Ohio to make her closing argument as to why she is the best candidate to take on Tim Ryan in November and is the only candidate in this race that you can trust to pursue the America First agenda. With more exciting events coming up in the next 5 days, I hope you’ll take a few minutes to learn more.
---
| | **Get Out and Vote**
---
Our amazing grassroots army has made over 1.5 million voter contacts and now it’s time for our supporters to get out and vote. Our team is working hard to get our targeted voters to the polls and that includes you.
---
---
It’s not too late to get out and vote early for Jane before Tuesday. Early vote centers across Ohio are open this weekend to save you a trip on Tuesday. You can find out where your county’s early vote center is [here](http://links.janetimkenforohio.com/u/click?_t=d33702f99bd24ab29d9d703faac4f8a3&_m=ebc7aef72be04905a99cd6a5fefa4520&_e=Pl31uzB2zEugguLP7ISPgNwjAmvyPFhU1nFaIGRupyWhOR8lxsTh9tybRb0iFQgkC3cgOnBFAtYLdkPiSf2xH3gOs7gbS46r1N0OhM23bn7QT5sOuaDnqU1biLU1U4NaTBxEIbNwcwVV-iIJf-AaMf6aMXDhCgAznLTbr4I_7Rn3aYIuOIU0l-ARgouGG7ROplJaJlWE5PAvDvPBozJSjkwC9UQDdU3-ptl_D4KNkImq0Sunljsi-fpZRWkhdGaZPPr97G1_dhvVY4iyAAb-2aii9-zvGA6x7-Bx0pAsT5iBeh7-BnlcIk0JKtz4pnwc). And of course, if you want to go on Election Day, make sure you know where your polling location is by finding it [here](http://links.janetimkenforohio.com/u/click?_t=d33702f99bd24ab29d9d703faac4f8a3&_m=ebc7aef72be04905a99cd6a5fefa4520&_e=Pl31uzB2zEugguLP7ISPgOpeENWunpFQ_M96FemsVC4W5JfKh66T_n0fXxuEeZMtrHPXyR60NBbUHvXiMO6MDA3BWjdrYRZ15H__eeBNtkBGYl2EXGPvtRKlGUPq1UdHnJ1yAur4vA7CxvFg_G_PSEHvz4yNMUJ6kxVT-N3yfLwMoZYiOlHNJLLarGa6T3zomtIFJo9TyPitoErDfkN4iEORyIIGgEwCtf6B1cqZVLZ6nyfNcO-zrc5wOwrB-ZkMjyApt4c5fI3uIMDkqqT_tsvwws0pr8NMiYVfqJKycxMK-VP1ROANdqTDK3gHQ4mT).
---
**From the Trail**
---
Last Friday night, Jane joined the NRA Western Reserve in Lake County. It was great to be with so many fired up patriots and as your U.S. Senator, Jane will always protect your Second Amendment rights.
---
[](http://links.janetimkenforohio.com/u/click?_t=d33702f99bd24ab29d9d703faac4f8a3&_m=ebc7aef72be04905a99cd6a5fefa4520&_e=Pl31uzB2zEugguLP7ISPgIkB6UCO-urBRygCZNkFUsptrRYynGNH4X3rdeenSKjBvgCqdMDVGDVIoTZ6DWkaYX-ZdZ9ApGlU3e4OniOCoAzcyQp3zZWz-33IAtosJO3SMia4rnn1r0oocNeSMH18l_dLf0zo94hn6_0sWBlB0vQScNlkuDsdfSqwy6KphVxBH2nTfXesc7gs3SHZhjq1dx-frRuI-PoEBad3cDcvFXB5c9lluSCgQdw3DOuavvepgoxn2-tsgVNRi54zr5oZR-zer92pAe4tactEKhMpX04eAUEsieO1ogOJqsEjCNQ0Nku3rbt6Nx8o87zRvpcXtQ%3D%3D)
---
---
On Saturday, Jane made two stops across the state to fire up our best in the nation field program during a huge Saturday of voter contacts.
---
---
---
---
On Monday we were thrilled to be hosted by State Senator Bob Peterson for a great roundtable on agriculture policy and the many issues Ohio farmers face from the Biden Administration. In the Senate, Jane will be a champion for Ohio agriculture.
---
[](http://links.janetimkenforohio.com/u/click?_t=d33702f99bd24ab29d9d703faac4f8a3&_m=ebc7aef72be04905a99cd6a5fefa4520&_e=Pl31uzB2zEugguLP7ISPgD0_Bz9HlVbt1G2gQc1oAMd56BYCY9YjaPOSoibuoeMoF8PUBwtqKD1HeCjN0oWtAmwqUVPVJkflMk8t-taHDxnjnm4_eOlVC3Jwc6eKH0Ai84asrn4sA9iJURPz7j35kXvk03hmV0GsUFTr_fP0rtUOP-_t1NIArJ5iGbWwG3vzLXg98fNk6JvtYSteRimqodVt-1LHFUxiyCHsdPQ4YTP67SFP-nV-MxrUuDdYPd3frOu2mtEZ3cbRenkuPViAzZiY7OsRIfo9g73zZ5-5V7rLIvQA9MHWs35NzQulKgJEjfTTTp-tu6O8VhgC_b9I_ZopF60AVQh1D26WwWPLTl3n29hjeuy9Hz3PRq8DeQt1)
---
---
Later that evening, Jane joined the Darke County Republican Party for their annual Lincoln Day Dinner with special guest Mark Meadows! An amazing crow of strong Ohio patriots.
---
---
---
On Tuesday, the Mom on a Mission tour took Jane to Lancaster. Jane discussed stopping Washington’s reckless spending, restarting America’s energy dominance, and getting political indoctrination out of our schools.
---
---
---
Jane was thrilled to join the Upper Arlington Conservative Club later that night. Franklin County needs conservative fighters to push conservative solutions and that starts with groups just like this.
---
---
On Wednesday, Jane toured Freeport Press in New Philadelphia. Freeport Press, like so many manufacturers & businesses, is having issues with the supply chain crisis. Jane will fight to bring our supply chains home to America so we aren’t relying on products oceans away.
---
---
Jane then stopped by Allied Machine & Engineering, a leading manufacturer in Dover, to talk with leaders and workers. From manufacturers big and small, Jane hears constantly we don’t have enough skilled workers. As Senator, Jane has a plan to strengthen Ohio’s workforce and train for the jobs needed!
---
---
On Thursday afternoon, our great supporters from the Dayton area hosted a meet and greet with voters from the area. Jane has such great supporters in the Dayton area who are fired up about the future of our country.
---
---
---
The Harrison County GOP hosted their annual Lincoln Day Dinner on Thursday night. These voters want a leader to combat inflation, secure the border, and stand up for parents and kids over bureaucrats and politicians!
---
---
---
| | **Join Jane to Close Out the Primary**
---
With just days left in the campaign, there are still plenty of opportunities to support Jane throughout the state. Join Jane as she finishes the campaign strong with events across Ohio.
---
---

clean_body: Jane Timken for Ohio Update| | | https:// | | Dear Peter, As we head into the last weekend of the campaign, Jane continues to work hard to earn the vote of Ohio Republican primary voters. With 35 events over the last 12 days of the campaign, Jane is crisscrossing Ohio to make her closing argument as to why she is the best candidate to take on Tim Ryan in November and is the only candidate in this race that you can trust to pursue the America First agenda. With more exciting events coming up in the next 5 days, I hope you’ll take a few minutes to learn more. | | Get Out and Vote Our amazing grassroots army has made over 1.5 million voter contacts and now it’s time for our supporters to get out and vote. Our team is working hard to get our targeted voters to the polls and that includes you. It’s not too late to get out and vote early for Jane before Tuesday. Early vote centers across Ohio are open this weekend to save you a trip on Tuesday. You can find out where your county’s early vote center is . And of course, if you want to go on Election Day, make sure you know where your polling location is by finding it . From the Trail Last Friday night, Jane joined the NRA Western Reserve in Lake County. It was great to be with so many fired up patriots and as your U.S. Senator, Jane will always protect your Second Amendment rights. On Saturday, Jane made two stops across the state to fire up our best in the nation field program during a huge Saturday of voter contacts. On Monday we were thrilled to be hosted by State Senator Bob Peterson for a great roundtable on agriculture policy and the many issues Ohio farmers face from the Biden Administration. In the Senate, Jane will be a champion for Ohio agriculture. Later that evening, Jane joined the Darke County Republican Party for their annual Lincoln Day Dinner with special guest Mark Meadows! An amazing crow of strong Ohio patriots. On Tuesday, the Mom on a Mission tour took Jane to Lancaster. Jane discussed stopping Washington’s reckless spending, restarting America’s energy dominance, and getting political indoctrination out of our schools. Jane was thrilled to join the Upper Arlington Conservative Club later that night. Franklin County needs conservative fighters to push conservative solutions and that starts with groups just like this. On Wednesday, Jane toured Freeport Press in New Philadelphia. Freeport Press, like so many manufacturers & businesses, is having issues with the supply chain crisis. Jane will fight to bring our supply chains home to America so we aren’t relying on products oceans away. Jane then stopped by Allied Machine & Engineering, a leading manufacturer in Dover, to talk with leaders and workers. From manufacturers big and small, Jane hears constantly we don’t have enough skilled workers. As Senator, Jane has a plan to strengthen Ohio’s workforce and train for the jobs needed! On Thursday afternoon, our great supporters from the Dayton area hosted a meet and greet with voters from the area. Jane has such great supporters in the Dayton area who are fired up about the future of our country. The Harrison County GOP hosted their annual Lincoln Day Dinner on Thursday night. These voters want a leader to combat inflation, secure the border, and stand up for parents and kids over bureaucrats and politicians! | | Join Jane to Close Out the Primary With just days left in the campaign, there are still plenty of opportunities to support Jane throughout the state. Join Jane as she finishes the campaign strong with events across Ohio. clean_body: We need a real businesswoman in Washington to clean up the mess Peter, Nobody works harder than my wife, Erika. That’s why she is the absolute best choice to be your next Congresswoman from Florida. I have to be honest, she is incredibly strong-willed and doesn’t like asking for help too often. That’s why I am reaching out to you today. The campaign has fallen $2,480 short of its goal this month. So, Elections have consequences – we can’t just stand idly by as Democrats wreak havoc on our country. Our goal to close the gap is very ambitious, but I know grassroots supporters like you understand the importance of this election. We have a very real chance of flipping this seat from blue to RED. I know it would mean the world to Erika, but most importantly, it will be the best investment for the 7th Congressional District of Florida. We need a real leader at the wheel – Thank you, Paul Benfield | | | | ---|---|--- Paid for by Erika Benfield for Congress

**Let Freedom Tweet 📱
**
You probably know that I like to tweet—a lot. It’s a good way to communicate and yes—help—people in real time. But Twitter—or any platform—doesn’t work if people don’t have free speech. And it’s not free speech if you’re not allowed to see it, like it, retweet it, and reply to it.

Liberals are freaking out, but I, for one, am very excited about Elon Musk [buying](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=589982e0f1294a2393633d998a92e686&_e=yidB7d-b-X0cxjVahBFRXDTZBGBQxgDELe0GrMSrg2b7Oxs3UKhZAJXEpe7C-AU7ILbtuOWYm5j8BEs3-lQBkKO-kIPLdhQERgcC3AibIdnQP6Q7s64uW4yFzqz1xNyzygSyy-x2ZF14aVNjZlCHAMM_qG6BeIpDmc1YGnLhMTes4QF4e77qdCUk0q-Byy1mZaTUCG-OHVOsQslbwerabaIrrR7qA1n650x9qicKv-JeyKf2b4JJu682svKqyIZsRCbQP288cxl5jEG1bSRQVnzq9vEm2xlf5xbeSfcCRAIuKTreVP7NmfhBMGe2FKTIYVpU0vKnMlYAI15YwcCszQ%3D%3D) Twitter.

For too long, Big Tech has [stifled conservative voices](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=589982e0f1294a2393633d998a92e686&_e=yidB7d-b-X0cxjVahBFRXGgAzhp86300d3pXVflr7B8Vr8aiy0Vucc8l5gCQ3Jrw-UgF4DDqU49ORRSb3YymVsMqCUvtjiS7No-hr1Hb134pl_b6cc8dT65uPNbbzh2NrnML7gCovcUdGRFeQPp96bKiZ0G-wGuLiXmnuXMrsBbRuFtehXbF11di74QCy_WJRbQtyw_5CObxoIIJH68ILxfnnX0ATF5XV5K9K20GAo6QCqq4WXAUV0B-kXPoMkxCk0-DpfvXjv0Z0mf-zHbB3RZvrYsYwDIigRPQra2h8xP4e61m6qFv_hbyoCNBRST1h4H9cy5fkMHZvGurQvNaOw%3D%3D) to appease the liberals’ woke agenda. Mind you, the Twitter bureaucrats have no problem [letting the ayatollahs in Iran](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=589982e0f1294a2393633d998a92e686&_e=yidB7d-b-X0cxjVahBFRXHVpzEopxlUN-oUTMcnor2w7W_qV0wUU8l5RuKgXrEOf54ulgfJwNi76wfjvJlSRLGY0GVxxvNrAdOQrVO2vcsAL93EJfxSdzCHvAdOSUz_HQdU77XXSL0K009DHNcrE5zeU05QiaDVOTYQwpKoI6zrBOElbABBOWLyuOdvKOrc83XhMiKnmgvbcHlYXWN6i3BKiTFJvK3wAR0rMbOdktNvF15pyMIlzKs2CuHF35rq81HnzX484AXMDxyr3cWWw5xAAXIT4oCtnow7yd6FgJLJioCI9f2L7v6Swy1IekbJoih_qdUGVtKU9b5x9AMSKqDRG-wotQhhUsitZPPijG3F7vDDPWY4hA2orRnv5_0WKTMnWx5m9l3XIt4NQ9ioaMeP0SANigvxOOYoMzKGr3WX38ziSTyZD1m_QJXtFUMfiInvFcKorIuwFzdM9RySW4Q%3D%3D) and the [communists in China](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=589982e0f1294a2393633d998a92e686&_e=yidB7d-b-X0cxjVahBFRXB58WutrAnqZKXviAxk06nQb_pyv39_wCGhOuH1ZVcWcOYFkdd2Bq2y9loYo7Jaa_4d09bXJXU2qPjt9F5yYqbsyKvewDiD26YiBNeNPk2XeqbzdySoib2zg4CrB-0GSdYHNn0CO-ctf9Rz7IYWZNCsz22of-bUdCYl4vq5xVVjAadh8epTiah_xik1GPR-eA4l3eLoNK6f380zKj2odtC2pOVW9aNGzkXEeFvUNhkON6oEF5whlf2cwH06EtLBJm-n7KzolqoJR77yfrp0BxUn45F4o1W6iMoa1JypFzxWKSqS8pk2NqGjXZobl5aY94YhxDu56w79LcKL3Se66Q4E%3D) say whatever the heck they want.

Free speech isn’t a conservative issue—at least it shouldn’t be. Everyone benefits from open dialogue, even if you don’t agree with what people are saying. That’s what makes America so great. Censorship is just plain un-American.

Now, liberals are [threatening](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=589982e0f1294a2393633d998a92e686&_e=yidB7d-b-X0cxjVahBFRXJifUhB48mQzyFnqUDWyXo5tSnrPgjphaiWfCYPdBXbqKhbTwOfQjbHUSB-qMdz7OHWjrgON9PqJt3zWZnZ-rIFyBJk0nacUsL5Hpd51XTsFIKanJc8NX3W0b6aNsoIkheKzq7J98qWyred16YDF_08DLlmi3sWezJenZgiqTVEBKNMXXQBJgCiBJtjVjPKOz7eKzhibwKmRurFRN6PFj9Bd1mGQZ3o07QIlvzuTFkBEKA6r5LIagZO7O62ushIGkK7tJOwA83UnPl9eril5-Wo3F19otkcKopLsY7dif7T2oyTusqSABaRviPjQ1SITyBQMN9TvPxKCseOiBTZHX3c%3D) to leave Twitter because they can’t handle a platform that is truly free and impartial. I have one thing to say to that: Don’t let the door hit you on the way out.

The [First Amendment](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=589982e0f1294a2393633d998a92e686&_e=yidB7d-b-X0cxjVahBFRXNdMe669rwY-GcBpvzdro6XY5Rmhpx_qoekU6vfKhPWoJo23mA6SsUMvRebVKcuCy2V_Gj8lOEWkbtXLn-s5r-2hdXLr5YQAQGYHMkT7G2VkU6yTU9Z1dGGydKN5LIhqhtJct6VhfbRF70cyPKNMgQw1WCfvkZW5aWwA1HC0Tv6yo89KCcy2gQudNE4xOtBW52WYk-mAg4giiafcGgdpehWDsW3IU4my5qo0cBE4Flv2rERP647YuerQR91lR-732t_2te0RbFBDREwXPLxex6bvS9xGyRu_a942hWbpBy1G) wasn’t written to protect popular opinions. It was written to protect **all** opinions. The Founders trusted people to make up their own minds. [Silicon Valley ](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=589982e0f1294a2393633d998a92e686&_e=yidB7d-b-X0cxjVahBFRXGgAzhp86300d3pXVflr7B-J_WrQcXeCHhjwwDlcqV50L26rxAcyM5j2_vtdz8wJpcLyZJtT-NZ7hpEifpLpC7I-liqW_efe7iE7-mEcY7QOsF-CRN5_RpXj8dIlZFTQCIZP7lyqnRWsoUqPiZ0O0iFfmPI8LbcWpRpYwFSLniOcnr8N8TKQ21_rPt9zjRkZGjsdiUqbftC4a-4303H0vReMRlt9kf5NjF1arspsgplN96Z_FksR86t3psd7zJYZF4bR4WfL3qmMSgnWxOiNFNlh8-x6zdypisxeYdt5FAWTDyqIAmhmWrCangVzPfg3j7bwzXgfDWNVtZ22sELXTro%3D)[millionaires](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=589982e0f1294a2393633d998a92e686&_e=yidB7d-b-X0cxjVahBFRXGgAzhp86300d3pXVflr7B-J_WrQcXeCHhjwwDlcqV50L26rxAcyM5j2_vtdz8wJpcLyZJtT-NZ7hpEifpLpC7I-liqW_efe7iE7-mEcY7QOsF-CRN5_RpXj8dIlZFTQCJKvQ4q02HHSAxfBzn1kAcKumJv3ejX_MNGoLQhq8iDjwoOyCEOOHI39GkAdvwogm1SPzEKmfrOFnG6bo1h0aR-OZ16d3S_-7Oepne6iL5GGY7XTDrU86Vx-xunKYFzPpqjyoNkXo9749zc4-wIGNLq9jrAIS0KPgwHELLHMl_QfxsqC4s0SjOsiNRgdJyO6Lod1a30jy_ofyxX6SeGhf_U%3D) should stick to computer coding, not speech codes.

## #Covfefe is back...
In case you missed the story behind this tweet going viral, you can read all about it and more in _The Briefing_ , but here's the excerpt on #covfefe: _Trump’s opinions on controversial issues were pretty transparent. Anyone who wanted to know what he was thinking only had to read his tweets. Keeping an eye out for his early morning, late-night, and weekend tweets was part of my new world order. I soon learned that there were two kinds of Trump tweets. There were the early morning and late-night tweets that were pure and unfiltered Trump when he had no staff around him. Then there were the business-hour tweets that were filtered through or drafted by the social media director, Dan Scavino. The former often caused me trouble because the press would latch onto any statements they saw as potentially embarrassing or controversial. The latter, on the other hand, were typically incisive and confronta- tional, but constructive. Dan Scavino was an invaluable editor for Trump, but he couldn’t be on call twenty-four hours a day. One exam- ple of a late-night tweet that got a lot of media, but was really rather harmless and amusing, was this famous fragment, issued at 12:06 a.m. from the president: “Despite the constant negative press covfefe.”_ _I assumed he meant “coverage,” and his thumbs simply hit the wrong button. But the minute I saw it, I said to myself, “Oh brother, here we go.” I would later see how even the most trivial events could go viral in the media. I later assured reporters in the most serious tone, “Only the president and other select people know what that means.”_

I’m raising money to help find a cure for for pancreatic cancer by walking in the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network’s annual PurpleStride. Tomorrow, I’ll be walking with my family in memory of my father, Michael Spicer.I’ve raised just over $10,000 so far, would really appreciate your help in reaching $12,000. Thank you! | | | | | | | | | #Covfefe is back... In case you missed the story behind this tweet going viral, you can read all about it and more in The Briefing , but here's the excerpt on #covfefe: Trump’s opinions on controversial issues were pretty transparent. Anyone who wanted to know what he was thinking only had to read his tweets. Keeping an eye out for his early morning, late-night, and weekend tweets was part of my new world order. I soon learned that there were two kinds of Trump tweets. There were the early morning and late-night tweets that were pure and unfiltered Trump when he had no staff around him. Then there were the business-hour tweets that were filtered through or drafted by the social media director, Dan Scavino. The former often caused me trouble because the press would latch onto any statements they saw as potentially embarrassing or controversial. The latter, on the other hand, were typically incisive and confronta- tional, but constructive. Dan Scavino was an invaluable editor for Trump, but he couldn’t be on call twenty-four hours a day. One exam- ple of a late-night tweet that got a lot of media, but was really rather harmless and amusing, was this famous fragment, issued at 12:06 a.m. from the president: “Despite the constant negative press covfefe.” I assumed he meant “coverage,” and his thumbs simply hit the wrong button. But the minute I saw it, I said to myself, “Oh brother, here we go.” I would later see how even the most trivial events could go viral in the media. I later assured reporters in the most serious tone, “Only the president and other select people know what that means.” | | | | | | | | Stories I’m reading... It’s playing out as I thought it was going to play out.” Read the story [HERE](http://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=1c81ce1c3d21431991916d8f36be9e49&_m=c1b6925f82e94465b5520fff3d52bf7b&_e=glX7hlfbF4TR60bcwtWjXhTpfNp0fJExExeU4MKiv2yk8D7wuwYEWSJ7Vbzq_Jhc8suL1BKGU8xaivWqHbO4iLgHLkHtyc-Pfp5npsw5YA8Uls71IyhF3bDgXJc6hRxBq-HSq7eAqK_IYZtj46HIwVAbdP_IsS3GuGUukjWUKyEklNBIFVc358I-aGFnFXROPlVl6k5EY7q29kAovC90rU4b0ner8up_x3zZe-oUWPb6pA51fE6qxcnyRTwDhzoGIh95AJ412mSj3Y1FATMDusoBKuwHMdRloo1v365GDruZB7aOj0F69jaPdyWT-XnQ).

Matt joined nationally syndicated conservative talk show host Erick Erickson to discuss the latest in the Ohio Senate race. Erickson kicked things by sharing his support for Matt, saying, “I hope he wins,” before praising Matt’s conservative credentials and strong appeal in the general election. Dolan: “...we have outsiders, we have Marjorie Taylor Greene, Matt Gaetz coming into Ohio telling Ohioans how they should vote for J.D. Vance ... Josh [Mandel] is closing with Ted Cruz coming in. I mean, this is about Ohio, Erick. The next U.S. Senator from Ohio better know Ohio and know Ohio issues. That’s why I’m rising up in the polls and I’m going to finish first next Tuesday. I’m the one who has conservative results. I’m the one who doesn’t have to change his message to beat the Democrats.” Listen [HERE](http://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=1c81ce1c3d21431991916d8f36be9e49&_m=c1b6925f82e94465b5520fff3d52bf7b&_e=glX7hlfbF4TR60bcwtWjXszX6Bu5dic6JCsjX5eq_TtTxH_WELE7SRT3yxcQTJQ79cpfaOtSC7nXS7VHn18VYwxkg_JqftTaE5L9INA9QiNUYKx1hQFSrw6jlXMHkxJD5KyXw3XN4qNj4uPwGND6LvPEt870qUulF_Q4F2AF6bcLAvempedyqfT-BOTdlfLZskWRCglQ4CUNph2sOhYKe6QdB7TAQPUtNDOH0EFLOkKce5H6_zy4P7BAcC2B3fZy5YMdcWI7g7ABSNJGzv8Va4LIfEOr8yz-v6G0j-MI39A%3D).

The number of billionaires in the United States couldn’t even fill an apartment building, but the number of people they negatively impact is only growing.
# [](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/143?refcode=em20220429-2988-header&t=1&akid=2988%2E2526796%2EW81-Is)
Alexandria just took Elon Musk and other billionaires _to task_ , on Twitter, for their claims that the “extreme left” is taking over, when in reality our “extreme” agenda is simple: protect and lift up working families.
The truth is, billionaires are mad that our progressive movement — and, in turn, its agenda — are growing, since it’s the conservative candidates they fund who allow them to continue building more wealth.
Enough is enough. As Alexandria tweeted, the number of billionaires in the United States couldn’t even fill an apartment building, but the number of people they negatively impact is only growing. [Click here to make a contribution to help our movement fight back against corporate greed and its control in Washington.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/aoc-email-20220429?refcode=em20220429-2988-P_FND_EOM_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&refcode2=2988_2526796_W81-Is&akid=2988%2E2526796%2EW81-Is)

Here’s the “extreme far-left” agenda:
* We believe that medicine and accessing health care shouldn’t bankrupt you;
* Wages should be liveable and be enough to cover rent and basic necessities;
* And that Wall Street companies and massive corporations shouldn’t profit off mass surveillance, a manufactured housing crisis, and caging people.

Alexandria is fighting for an agenda that puts working people first — one that ensures families can get the health care they need and afford to put food on their tables, and builds an equitable future for the next generations. That’s why we need to keep her in Congress.
[Tomorrow is our April fundraising deadline and we’re counting on the support of our grassroots movement — that means YOU — to help us ensure we have the resources we need to reelect Alexandria this year and keep her in Congress fighting for an agenda that centers our lives and our communities. body:
April was one of our best months yet. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/6e51bece4cb7/saying-goodbye?e=10c1db3257)
---
| | [ ](https://beckyforutah.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cb6d6dad27d2e4a00e5c44525&id=4dcc17977a&e=10c1db3257)
---
|
---
| Dear Friend,

This month, we planted the seeds, trimmed the weeds, and now, **we’re ready to blossom!**

We are so excited to be starting**another month on the campaign!** April brought us the end to a **successful convention season, hundreds of new and amazing volunteers,** and so many great opportunities to **meet voters across the state. **

With warmer temperatures and**just a few weeks to the Republican primary,** May is sure to bring more **energy and excitement to this race. **Before we say goodbye to April, **here are some of this month’s highlights! **
---
| |
---
* We secured our spot on the **Republican primary ballot!** After months of collecting, we submitted a **total of 43,000 signatures** to the Lt. Governor's Office. We couldn’t have done it without **our amazing volunteers** who helped gather signatures from **every county in the state! **

---
| |
---
* We attended **state-wide county conventions!** Convention season was a fantastic opportunity to talk with voters, try some local treats, and discover the **rich history being kept alive in our communities.**

---
| |
---
* We spent time with our **volunteers and their families** at our Volunteer Celebration! Thanks to them, our campaign has reached **thousands of voters across the state,** and I cant wait to see **what goals they reach next.**

---
| |
---
* We had a fantastic time at the **State convention!** I was privileged to be named the second-place candidate, affirming what we’ve known for the past 11-months—**we are the leading Republican challenger in this race!** Thank you to all staff, volunteers, and delegates who helped make our booth a welcoming space and **convention day a success!**

---
| As always, **thank you for your ongoing support.** We can’t express our gratitude enough, and I’m confident that **May will bring growth and success with you by my side.**
---

Our state needs a real conservative leader with an Ohio first agenda. I will fight for the people of this great state, but I can’t do this without your help. Will you stand with me? | | | Thank you, Jim Renacci Candidate for Governor of Ohio | | Paid for by Renacci for Ohio |

My mom taught me that if you have faith just the size of a mustard seed,
you can move a mountain. And I have faith that we can defeat Rand Paul and
take back Kentucky for us all. But if we’re going to do this, I can’t do
it alone.

Think about it this way: if 2 people from every zip code reading this
email chipped in $5 — we can close a significant gap in our goal. [ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cb-em-20220429-2?refcode=em20220429-1846&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1001&refcode2=1846_346206_v-OUyT&akid=1846%2E346206%2Ev-OUyT ]Will
you be the one from 18326 to step up and pitch in?

Peter,
it’s important to me that I share with
you exactly how your donation and the money from our April fundraising
goal will be used.

I don’t take your generosity or money for granted — we’re putting every
penny toward a movement that works for all of us.

This is how we’re going to invest your donation and win this U.S. Senate
seat. (Usually, campaigns keep this kind of information close to the
chest. But we’re not doing things the way they’ve always been done.)

* The primary: Our primary is on May 17th. Winning our primary is the
first step in replacing Rand Paul and we want to make sure a record
number of voters turn out for this election. It’s important we show
our grassroots strength and send a clear signal that this progressive
movement is rising up.

* Building the biggest grassroots organizing program ever in Kentucky:
For too long, there’s been this myth that Kentucky is a red state. But
it’s not. It’s an unorganized, disenfranchised, and exploited state.
It’s one of the only states in the country with Republican senators
and a Democratic governor. Where the number of people who don’t vote
outnumber those who do. And when you look at recent political trends
all the numbers show that the tides are turning: we have a real chance
to elect bold progressive leadership in Kentucky and make history
this election.

* Reaching out to voters from the hood to the holler: Building a winning
movement means we need to mobilize voters in all 120 counties of
Kentucky. This kind of widespread outreach is going to require
significant investments in voter outreach, volunteer recruitment, and
our digital strategy.

That’s why we set a goal to raise 7,500 grassroots donations by the end of
the month. If we all chip in what we can — our campaign will have the
funds to continue building this historic movement in Kentucky and
transform our politics.

Thank you,

Charles
